title: Grateful Dead Live at Family Dog at the Great Highway on 1969-08-30
venue: Family Dog at the Great Highway
lineage: Master Soundboard Reel > Cass > DAT > CD > EAC (secure) > mkwACT > SHN (no SBE's)

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard recording that captures a soaring 1969 set highlighted by a 29‑minute Dark Star and daring, creative jams.
ai_review.review: The tape offers surprisingly crisp, high‑fidelity stereo mix for a late‑60s show, with only minor wobble at the tail end of China Cat. Musically the performance is a psychedelic tour de force – Jerry’s inventive guitar (even through a broken string) drives an unforgettable Dark Star, while St Stephen, The Eleven and Easy Wind provide extra fireworks despite a few uneven moments on China Cat and Doin’ That Rag.

ai_rating.rationale: Average star rating is 4.3; most reviewers praise both the music (especially Dark Star) and the recording quality, with only a handful of low‑star critiques.

recording_quality.technical_notes: High‑quality stereo mix with crisp instrument separation; occasional tape distortion/wobble at the very end of China Cat and beginning of Doin' That Rag, but overall superb for a 1969 source.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A sprawling first disc capped by a monumental Dark Star, followed by an off‑kilter second disc that still delivers strong transitions and a compelling close; the set feels adventurous despite occasional rough edges.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for brilliant, creative lead work; his tone, feedback leads and broken‑string recovery are highlighted throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is noted as “making a statement” with tight, melodic jams that lock in with the guitars.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s organ vamp during the broken‑string moment receives specific commendation; overall keyboard work is described as solid.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drum crash landings and a standout drum solo are mentioned, adding power to The Eleven.
